Original unrestricted S18, unchanged, as context and conventions:
All manifolds are connected and compact. Write dd^c=(i/(2 pi))partial barpartial. Use genuine canonical quasi-psh representatives. For a smooth real (1,1) form theta, PSH(X,theta) means theta+dd^c u>=0. Ordinary order u preceq v means u<=v+C and equivalence means mutual order, including the canonical values at common poles. Extended products mean non-pluripolar Monge-Ampere products with smooth-background corrections. A big background admits a genuine strict current theta+dd^c u>=epsilon h for some Hermitian h and epsilon>0. BMP means v_+(h)<infinity, where v_+(h) and v_-(h) are the supremum and infimum of integral(h+dd^c u)^n over all bounded h-psh u. Positive lower mass means v_-(h)>0; it is distinct from BMP. Define I(tu) by local integrability of |g|^2 exp(-tu), with no extra factor 2. Ideal equivalence means equality at every real t>0. P_theta[u]_I is the usc supremum of theta-psh v<=0 ideal-equivalent to u. P_theta[u] is the ordinary singularity envelope, the usc supremum of theta-psh v<=0 with v preceq u. The lower and upper singularity volumes are the infimum and supremum of the extended mass over all v ordinarily equivalent to u in the specified background, not the raw mass of one representative. Original S18 is a research direction whose precise invariant is to be formulated: develop moving-product or birational volume data for smooth big possibly nonclosed backgrounds, accounting for imposed poles, residual positivity and differential background data. Specify the invariant, its smooth-gauge and modification behavior before asserting a volume formula. Distinguish upper singularity volume from fixed-density Gauduchon variational volume. For a smooth strictly positive probability mu, define D_mu(gamma)=integral((gamma^n/mu)^((n-1)/n))mu and lambda_mu(theta)=inf_(gamma>0,dd^c gamma^(n-1)=0) integral theta wedge gamma^(n-1)/D_mu(gamma), with V_mu=lambda_mu^n on its nonnegative domain. The infimum uses all smooth Gauduchon tests. On a smooth-positive representative segment theta_s=theta-s eta, its derivative is minus integral eta wedge gamma_s^(n-1)/D_mu(gamma_s) for a minimizing test; integration gives the actual subtraction cost. The geometric extension up to a nef endpoint beyond a closed positive core is P14, and is not assumed solved here. Finite effective real divisor residuals have known explicit mass polynomials and Gauduchon variations. Closed class-C restricted invariants, closed Kahler positive products and classical volume differentiability are known within their own hypotheses. Nonclosed degeneration can have irrational or oscillatory orders and modification jumps, so the closed numerical formulas do not transfer automatically. Gauge transport theta prime=theta+dd^c f pairs with u prime=u-f, preserving the actual current, whereas changing a normalized representative can change raw nonclosed mass. No proposed moving invariant, geometry or proof is supplied.

Proposed statement-only targets, all requiring proof:
# S18: root-developed statement-only targets, not a proof

These proposed scoped statements originate in a separately identified root
candidate, not in autonomous Xean discovery. No proof, construction of
approximating competitors, original article, private note or prior verdict is
supplied to an independent reconstructor. Every statement needs verification.
The unrestricted S18 programme remains open.

Use dd^c=i partial barpartial/(2 pi). Let w be the probability Fubini--Study
form on P1, X=P1 x P1, w_i its two pullbacks, and p a point of the first
factor. Let G_p<=0 be its genuine Green potential, dd^c G_p=[p]-w,
with max G_p=0. Fix 0<alpha<1 and put U=1-(1-G_p)^alpha and u=pr1^*U.
All potentials are genuine canonical quasi-psh functions. Equivalence means
bounded difference, with inequalities interpreted canonically at common poles.

For c>=alpha and a>0 a smooth function on the first factor, set
theta=c w1+a w2. Define

  sigma_minus(theta,u)=inf_{v theta-psh, v~u} MA_theta^ext(v)(X),
  sigma_plus(theta,u)=sup_{v theta-psh, v~u} MA_theta^ext(v)(X).

The products are the catalogue's finite-level non-pluripolar products with
smooth-background corrections. The extrema concern every full-variable
ordinary-equivalent theta-psh v, not merely separated potentials.

## Target A: an actual nonanalytic imposed type and full mass optimization

The form theta is smooth positive, big, and nonclosed whenever a is
nonconstant. u is an admissible theta-psh representative with a genuine
unbounded nonanalytic pole along {p} x P1, zero Lelong numbers, and trivial
multiplier ideals I(tu)=O_X for every real t>0. Every theta-psh v~u has
positive finite extended top mass, and

  MA_theta^ext(v)(X)=integral_X theta^2+2 integral_X v dd^c theta,
  sigma_minus(theta,u)=2c min a,
  sigma_plus(theta,u)=2c max a.

Both extremal values are approached by actual admissible representatives of
that exact ordinary type. Prove the global optimization against arbitrary
fiber-dependent rough competitors and every actual product passage, without assuming a finite first moment; it is
insufficient to compute just separated smooth products. No general nonclosed
intersection-invariance theorem is permitted as a black box.

## Target B: the separate fixed-density all-test variational formula

Let m>0 be smooth on the first factor, integral m w=1, and mu=m w1 w2.
For every smooth positive Gauduchon (1,1) test T with dd^c T=0 put
D_mu(T)=integral_X sqrt(T^2/mu) mu. The infimum below uses ALL such tests:

  lambda_mu(theta)=inf_T integral_X theta wedge T/D_mu(T),
  V_mu(theta)=lambda_mu(theta)^2=2c/H,
  H=integral_P1 (m/a)w.

It is attained by the smooth positive test
T=(g/a)w1+w2, where g=V_mu(theta)m/(2a).
The proof must establish both the unrestricted lower bound and actual
attainment, without an assumed PDE normalization formula. This volume depends
on m when a is nonconstant; the two singularity mass extrema in A do not.
They generally differ.

## Target C: actual moving subtraction, logarithmic endpoint, and scope

For a fixed m and a smooth positive segment
c_s=c-s d>=alpha, a_s=a-s b>0 (d real constant, b real smooth on P1),
let theta_s=c_s w1+a_s w2 and eta=d w1+b w2. Define H_s,V_s,g_s,T_s as
in B. Then

  d sqrt(V_s)/ds=-integral_X eta wedge T_s/D_mu(T_s).

Integration gives the exact full-test Gauduchon subtraction cost on every
compact subsegment, while sigma_minus=2c_s min a_s and
sigma_plus=2c_s max a_s remain separate data.

For the concrete case c=1, m=1, a=2+tau, where tau is the smooth standard
height on P1 with range [-1,1], subtract eta=w2. For 0<=s<1,

  sigma_minus=2(1-s), sigma_plus=2(3-s),
  V_s=4/log((3-s)/(1-s)).

At s=0 the raw zero-potential mass is 4 and the preceding three data are
2, 6 and 4/log 3. The endpoint theta_1 is smooth semipositive and nef,
is not big, and has all-test lambda_mu(theta_1)=0. The upper ordinary-type
mass tends to 4 although V_s tends to zero logarithmically. The endpoint
lies outside the big positive segment. This is an explicit example, not a
closure of general P08/P14/S18 or a claim that all lower-volume failures have
this geometry.

## Target D: exact gauge and pure modification laws

For smooth real f, theta'=theta+dd^c f, u'=u-f, v'=v-f transport the exact
currents and extended measures and preserve both ordinary-type extrema and
the fixed-density Gauduchon numerator. A moving smooth gauge has zero pairing
contribution to the subtraction cost against dd^c-closed tests.

For a proper modification pi:Y->X between smooth connected compact complex
manifolds, genuine pi^*theta-psh functions descend canonically, and pullback
is an inverse bijection with PSH(X,theta). Ordinary inequalities and types
correspond. For corresponding potentials,

  pi_* MA_(pi^*theta)^ext(pi^*v)=MA_theta^ext(v),

including the finite/infinite interpretation if that extension is asserted.
Thus the mass extrema are preserved for the PURE pullback background and type.
Prove canonical admissibility, extension across the center, and the actual
non-pluripolar measure law; exceptional curvature subtraction is a different
operation and no equality across such a jump is asserted. No equality of
fixed-density variational volumes for arbitrary smooth positive upstairs
probabilities is asserted, and pi^*mu is not called strictly positive.

For a single point blowup of the concrete projective surface, the pure

## Permitted primary-assessed closed foundations, not target proofs

For a compact Kahler manifold with a CLOSED strict Kahler background K,
finite Aubin--Mabuchi energy E1 is stable under making a potential less
singular and under adding finite constants, and implies full closed top
non-pluripolar mass integral K^n. For a full-mass potential, finite integral
(-v) MA_K(v) (after sup v=0) is equivalent to finite E1.
These are the exact qualitative applications of BEGZ, Acta Math.205(2010),
Definitions2.7/2.9, Propositions2.8/2.10/2.11 and Section2.3. They have been
separately primary-proof assessed for closed K, and supply neither a
nonclosed mass identity nor the target proof. Standard local bounded
Bedford--Taylor products, their decreasing continuity and non-pluripolar
locality are permitted foundational conventions from the original task.
No Siu divisor theorem, general nonclosed mass monotonicity or unproved
rooftop continuity is supplied.

The elementary canonical removable-singularity theorem for locally
bounded-above psh functions across a closed pluripolar set is also permitted;
Demailly, Complex Analytic and Differential Geometry, I.5.23--5.24,
with its complete proof, has been separately primary-assessed.


## Target E: the exact first-moment boundary, not a finiteness premise

For K=C(w1+w2), with C large enough that K>=theta and C>=alpha, the
actual closed non-pluripolar product of the reference u has full mass
integral K^2. Its first moment integral_X (-u) MA_K(u) is finite exactly
when alpha<1/2 and infinite for 1/2<=alpha<1, with logarithmic divergence
at alpha=1/2. Targets A--D hold throughout alpha in (0,1), without a finite
first-moment assumption. Establish this statement using actual measures.

## Additional exact primary-assessed closed comparison foundation

On a compact Kähler manifold, cohomologous closed positive (1,1) currents
with small unbounded locus have ordered non-pluripolar product classes when
their potentials have the corresponding ordinary singularity order.
Here small unbounded locus means local boundedness outside a closed locally
complete pluripolar set. Apply only with all these hypotheses established.
This is BEGZ, Acta Math.205(2010), Theorem1.16 (printed217--218), not an
assumption about nonclosed backgrounds or arbitrary unbounded loci.
The theorem's complete printed proof has been separately root-read. The
comparison is allowed closed background only, not any requested target.

Its positive trace measures against smooth forms give zero mass to pluripolar sets. Conversely a distribution with positive complex Hessian has a unique locally integrable genuine psh representative. Radial convolution decreases to that representative, holomorphic pullback is psh possibly identically minus infinity, and genuine representatives are determined by almost-everywhere values.
